summary: Intermittent p99 timeouts correlated with continuous-batcher entrainment under skewed tenant arrival patterns
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent p99 request timeouts (504/timeout) on hosted inference endpoints. Pattern appears during sustained, but uneven traffic from multiple tenants on a single dedicated shard. Impact: Several production API calls for NarrativeAI returned timeouts over a 3-hour window, resulting in visible errors to end users and an SLA incident. Environment: prod, dedicated shard srv-ded-11, us-east-1, serving-runtime v2.8.3, continuous-batcher enabled with default tenant weights. Observed behavior: p95 stable, p99 spikes and occasional stream disconnects correlate with periodic bursts of small requests from one high-frequency tenant followed by quiet periods from others. Hypothesis: Continuous batcher is becoming "entrained" (synchronized) to tenant burst cycles when tenant-level burst controls and KV-cache miss sequences align, causing batch windows to flush simultaneously and produce tail latency spikes. This is exacerbated when tenant burst smoothing is disabled and when KV-cache misses force model cache warms within the batch flush window. No evidence of GPU OOMs or scheduler backpressure in the observed period.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision a dedicated shard with continuous-batcher enabled and default tenant weights.
2) Generate sustained uneven traffic: Tenant A emits many short requests (avg 20 tokens) in tight bursts for 30s on/off cycles; Tenant B/C emit sparse long requests.
3) Observe per-tenant p99 latency on inference routes for 15-60 minutes using the Console traces and request logs.
4) Toggle tenant burst smoothing to ON and re-run to compare tails.

comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-09: Opened with customer-provided traces and Console links. Customer reports ~3% error rate during 09:00-12:00 window. Asked for sampling config and recent config changes.

SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-10: Initial triage shows batcher flushes clustering at ~12ms windows with high batch sizes during tenant A bursts. No scheduler level throttles. Hypothesis: temporal alignment between tenant A bursts and batcher linger causes large microbatches and KV cache miss amplification. Requesting reproducer workload from customer and enabling debug traces on shard.

Engineering (Priya Reddy) 2026-03-11: Added instrumentation to measure per-tenant arrival phase and batch flush timestamp jitter. Observed >85% of p99 spikes occur when two conditions met: (1) tenant burst on ramped in <200ms and (2) per-tenant KV cache miss rate >30% in same window.

Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12: Applied temporary workaround: enabled tenant burst smoothing on NarrativeAI dedicated shard and lowered per-tenant max_burst_tokens from 10k -> 4k. Customer reports reduction in observed errors during monitoring period.
Customer (NarrativeAI Ops) 2026-03-12: Confirmed decreased end-user errors after smoothing and lower burst limit. Asked for permanent mitigation plan.

SRE (Liam O'Connor) 2026-03-12: Scheduling a controlled A/B rollout of two mitigations: 1) tenant-burst smoothing by default and 2) prewarming KV-cache for tenants exhibiting >20% miss rate during bursts. Target: next maintenance window 2026-03-18.
investigation_notes: - Batcher trace histograms show multimodal flush intervals aligning with tenant burst cadence.
- KV-cache miss amplification: many small requests force model path cold-starts inside same microbatch leading to slightly longer per-token times that add up at p99.
- No indication of hardware contention (GPU metrics normal), suggests scheduling/queueing dynamics are root cause.
- Similar pattern reported in SUP-27654 but that focused on cross-tenant batch merging; here root cause is entrainment to a single tenant's burst pattern on a dedicated shard.
- Reproducer created using wrk-style driver that simulates on/off 30s bursts with 20-token short requests shows p99 >1s when smoothing disabled and KV miss rate high.
resolution: Temporary: enabled tenant burst smoothing and reduced per-tenant max_burst_tokens on affected shard (applied 2026-03-12). Customer observed immediate reduction in errors. Planned permanent fix: engineering to implement two changes: (1) adaptive batcher jitter to de-synchronize flush windows across tenant arrival phases, and (2) proactive KV-cache prefetch for tenants that exhibit bursty small-request patterns. A/B rollout scheduled for 2026-03-18 with monitoring dashboards and alert thresholds. Follow-up: update continuous-batcher runbook and add a checklist for dedicated shard placement of high-burst tenants.
